svg.title: ArcHive architecture
svg.desc: Who pays (AI agents through the MCP server, apps through the TypeScript SDK, people through the site and AskHive), what runs where (the operator's registrar and archive-node; five enclaves in Intel TDX VMs on Phala Cloud) and what Arc checks and records (admission through EnclaveRegistry, TdxAttestationModule and Automata's DCAP verifier; the verified level; payments with EIP-3009 split 95/0/5; bonds and slashing; verdicts in the ERC-8004 validation registry), with CCTP V2 bringing USDC to Arc. Steps 1 to 4: admit a machine, an agent pays per call, the enclave answers with a signed receipt and the operator settles, a lie is replayed, refuted and the bond seized.
svg.text: Sealed machines, open market. AI agents, apps and people pay per use in USDC for work in Intel TDX enclaves that Arc admits and pays on; a lie costs the operator's bond.
v3 · 14 contracts in service, all shown
½ bond a day, 10 USDC per product
slash: ½ reporter, ½ victim or network
thin: a read, or a call between contracts
Circle's CCTP V2 from the Bridge page:
burn there, mint USDC on Arc
